items.title: LLMs as a Cognitive Virus
items.summary: The article discusses how large language models (LLMs) can spread rapidly and influence human thought processes, likening their impact to that of a cognitive virus. This comparison highlights the potential for LLMs to significantly shape public opinion and individual beliefs on a wide scale, underscoring the need for awareness about their influence.
items.summary_detailed: A new study suggests that Large Language Models (LLMs) could be viewed metaphorically as a "cognitive virus," potentially altering human decision-making processes and information processing. Researchers from MIT and Harvard Universities are leading this investigation, which highlights concerns about the broader impact of LLMs on society, including potential ethical and psychological implications. This research could influence future guidelines and regulations for developing and deploying LLMs to ensure they do not negatively affect public cognition or privacy.
